comment: Authored hero-character features for the station's eleven referenced roles (Phase 6, decision D4). Written by scripts/make-npc-glb.mjs; the .glb files are reproduced byte for byte by re-running it, and scripts/tests/npc-assets.test.mjs holds every number below against the file on disk. glTF materials are DISCARDED on load - each part draws in the character material slot named here, so nothing in this manifest can add a shader program. 'roles' is the whole reason there are two files rather than eleven: which parts a role shows is a manifest decision, not a geometry one. 'bones' takes an ARRAY for a part authored across the centreline: a pair of hands bound to handR alone puts the left hand on the right wrist and folds the character in half the moment it moves an arm.

rifle.note: g1 - furred, one pauldron, crossed bandolier. The line archetype, so the plainest.

breaker.note: g3 - no pauldron, a single harness with lit nodes. A brawler, so nothing on the shoulder to catch.

scout.note: g2 - crested and spined, no armour at all. Fast and badly equipped, and it should look it.

lance.note: g4 - the most armoured: pauldron, dorsal spikes and forearm spikes.

vendor.note: n1 - working a stall, so a chest rig and no life-support pack.

guard.note: n2 - full rig, pack and lit chest panel.

loiterer.note: n3 - off duty. Belt and boots only, which is what makes the others read as on duty.

spectator.note: n5 - seated, watching. Rig without the pack, which would be in the way of a bench.

wanderer.note: n4 - carrying a pack because they are going somewhere.

lorekeeper.note: n6 - seated at a gateway with a lit panel to read from.

quest_manager.note: n7 - the dispatcher: everything, because they are the one you are meant to walk towards.
